title: Integrated wastewater and clinical genomic surveillance for high-resolution tracking of measles virus evolution and transmission
desc: Measles outbreaks have surged globally, challenging surveillance and control efforts. In South Africa, the 2024−2025 measles outbreak led to nearly 4,000 reported cases, triggering a nationwide vaccination campaign. However, tracking measles virus (MeV; species Morbillivirus hominis) transmission and evolution remains difficult at scale, particularly in settings with limited access to care, diagnostic testing and sequencing capacity. Wastewater can enable population-scale virus surveillance, but low MeV concentrations limit detection sensitivity and sequencing quality. Here we show that overcoming these technical challenges enables integrated wastewater and clinical genomic surveillance that expands the coverage and resolution of MeV monitoring. We developed a virus concentration and whole-genome sequencing (WGS) workflow and applied it to 4,502 wastewater samples collected across all nine provinces of South Africa during the 2024−2025 outbreak. Wastewater MeV genotype prevalence tracked clinical estimates, and phylogenetic analyses combining wastewater and clinical sequences revealed geographically structured transmission and previously undetected inter-provincial spread. WGS recovered transmission links not captured by the field standard approach, which targets a 450-nucleotide region of the nucleoprotein gene (N450), highlighting the importance of WGS to accurately characterize transmission dynamics. Our study provides a cost-effective and scalable genomic surveillance approach to support measles control and elimination.

title: A measurement noise scaling law for cellular representation learning
desc: Large genomic and imaging datasets can be used to train models that learn meaningful representations of cellular systems. Across domains, model performance improves predictably with dataset size and compute budget, providing a basis for allocating data and computation. Scientific data, however, are also limited by noise arising from factors such as molecular undersampling, sequencing errors and image resolution. Here we introduce mutual information with auxiliary signals as a metric of representation model performance and study its scaling with noise. By fitting more than 2,000 representation learning models across three data modalities (gene expression, sequence and image data), we show that noise defines a distinct axis along which performance improves. Noise scaling follows a logarithmic law. We derive the law from a model of noise propagation, and use it to define noise sensitivity and model capacity as benchmarking metrics. We show that protein-sequence representations tolerate error rates in modern sequencing data, whereas single-cell transcriptomic models remain noise limited at current measurement signal-to-noise ratio levels. Within transcriptomic cell-state representation learning models, we find that transformer-based models are more noise robust but less performant than variational autoencoders. Noise scaling metrics may support future model evaluation and experimental design.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Large Language Models Across the Heart Failure Care Pathway: A Narrative Review.
desc: [Journal of personalized medicine] Heart failure affects more than 64 million people worldwide and remains associated with high mortality and recurrent hospitalisation. Artificial intelligence (AI), including large language models (LLMs), is being evaluated across the care pathway, but evidence maturity varies by task. The aim of this narrative review was to appraise direct evidence for LLM applications in heart failure, distinguish it from supporting evidence for other AI methods and propose a risk-based framework for clinical evaluation and governance. The strongest direct LLM evidence concerns electronic health record extraction, document drafting, patient information and clinical trial endpoint adjudication. A small, randomised pilot evaluated supervised generative-AI-guided optimisation of guideline-directed medical therapy. Prospective case-finding and monitoring evidence largely concerns non-LLM AI. For conversational AI telemonitoring (a natural language interface with rule-based alerting), prospective evidence was limited to a single non-randomised controlled pilot. Performance depends on task definition, data completeness, human review and workflow adoption. Overall, LLMs can support clearly defined, supervised heart failure tasks, but current evidence does not justify autonomous high-stakes care. The evidence base is expanding but predominantly retrospective. Prospective trials, disease-specific benchmarks, equity assessment and regulatory engagement are prerequisites for safe clinical translation. Human oversight remains essential across all current-generation applications.

title: Learning the Malignant Transformation of Lung Adenocarcinoma Cells Using Explainable AI
desc: Tumor evolution in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) drives drug resistance and disease progression, yet the cellular transitions underlying the malignant transformation of cells remain poorly understood. Comparing this progression of cancer cells across patients is challenging owing to substantial inter-patient cell heterogeneity. Here, based on single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) data of 227 patients with LUAD including 422,727 tumor cells, we conducted a comprehensive investigation of tumor cell progression and developed Global Tumor Time (GTT), a continuous measure of tumor cell progression across patients. GTT provided a scalable and biologically meaningful metric of tumor progression that aligned with clinicopathological, transcriptomic and spatial characteristics of malignancy and demonstrated robust prognostic performance (C-index = 0.60), which was further validated in two external datasets comprising snRNA-seq (C-index = 0.66) and bulk RNA sequencing (C-index = 0.61). Using explainable AI to investigate the molecular correlates of GTT, we identified two distinct transcriptional programs associated with early and late progression states. These findings establish a scalable and interpretable framework for reconstructing malignant cell transformation across patients and allow for investigating the biology of tumor progression at single-cell resolution.

Performance of intracortical microelectrode arrays in people with implanted brain–computer interfaces over a 20-year period
desc: The silicon microelectrode ‘Utah’ array has enabled people with paralysis to control computer cursors, operate prosthetic limbs and communicate using high-performance brain–computer interfaces. However, reports so far have typically been limited to one or two individuals, with no systematic assessment of array longevity, decoding accuracy and day-to-day stability. Here we present a comprehensive 20-year evaluation of neural data from the BrainGate clinical trials, spanning 2,289 recording sessions, 20 arrays and 14 participants. On average, arrays successfully recorded neural spiking waveforms on 35.6% of electrodes, with a modest 7 percentage point decline over the recording period (up to 7.3 years). Using a ‘decoding signal-to-noise ratio’ (dSNR) metric, we found that 11 of 14 arrays provided meaningful movement decoding throughout participation (median dSNR >1), with three achieving >70% accuracy compared with able-bodied mouse control. We also found that dSNR increased approximately logarithmically with the number of electrodes, providing a pathway for scaling performance. While longevity exceeded previous nonhuman primate studies, achieving peak performance consistently may require further improvements.

title: Accelerating inverse materials design using generative diffusion models with reinforcement learning
desc: Diffusion models promise to accelerate materials design by directly generating novel structures with desired properties, but existing approaches such as conditional generation typically require expensive and substantial labelled data (>10,000) and lack adaptability. Here we present MatInvent, a general and efficient reinforcement learning workflow that optimizes diffusion models for goal-directed crystal generation. By formulating equivariant denoising as a multistep decision-making problem, MatInvent leverages policy gradient with reward-weighted Kullback–Leibler regularization, including experience replay and diversity filters to enhance optimization efficiency and sample diversity. For single-objective designs, MatInvent rapidly converges to target values within 60 iterations (~1,000 property evaluations) across electronic, magnetic, mechanical, thermal and physicochemical properties. Furthermore, MatInvent achieves robust optimization in design tasks with multiple conflicting properties, successfully proposing low-supply-chain-risk magnets and high-κ dielectrics. Compared with state-of-the-art methods, MatInvent exhibits comparable or superior generation performance under specified property constraints while markedly reducing the demand for property computation. Compatible with diverse diffusion model architectures and property constraints, MatInvent could offer broad applicability in materials discovery.

title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer and Immunotherapy: A Review of the Emerging Uses and Current Challenges.
source: PubMed · International journal of molecular sciences
desc: [International journal of molecular sciences] Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide despite major therapeutic advances, including immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). Although a subset of patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) experiences durable long-term responses, currently available predictive biomarkers, including programmed death ligand-1 (PD-L1) expression, have limited ability to reliably distinguish responders from non-responders. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) have emerged as powerful approaches for extracting clinically meaningful patterns from complex, high-dimensional datasets spanning pathology, liquid biopsy, imaging, and integrated multimodal data. This narrative review examines current applications of AI in NSCLC immunotherapy across these complementary data modalities and evaluates the evidence supporting their clinical translation. Particular attention is given to the methodological limitations of existing studies and to the emerging shift from single-modality biomarkers toward dynamic and multimodal prediction. Although AI-based approaches show potential to complement established biomarkers, limitations in validation, generalizability, and prospective evidence currently restrict their clinical implementation.

title: BYSTER: multimodal graph learning resolves bystander versus tumor-specific T cell states in the tumor immune microenvironment
desc: Bystander T cells infiltrate tumors without recognizing tumor antigens and constitute a substantial component of the tumor microenvironment. Whether they are passive residents or active participants in antitumor immunity, and how they influence immunotherapy response, remains poorly understood, largely because transcriptional states and T-cell receptor (TCR) sequences alone do not reliably resolve antigen specificity. Here, we developed BYSTER, a heterogeneous graph neural network that integrates transcriptional representations with paired TCR representations through cross-modal message passing at metacell and metaTCR resolution. Across three datasets with distinct definitions of tumor specificity, BYSTER achieved mean AUROCs of 0.729 to 0.920, outperforming unimodal and conventional multimodal baselines, and ablation analyses confirmed the contribution of cross-modal message passing. Application to lung and pancreatic cancer cohorts revealed distinct biological characteristics of the two predicted populations. Bystander T cells were enriched for naive and memory subsets and MAIT-like cells expressing SLC4A10, and exhibited inflammatory and cellular stress-associated programs, including TNF signaling via NF-{kappa}B and hypoxia. Notably, these transcriptional patterns were consistent across lung and pancreatic cancers, with tumor-specific T cells showing enrichment of cell cycle and proliferation-associated programs in both cancer types. Spatial analyses further revealed distinct inferred communication patterns, with bystander T cells showing associations with inflammatory ligand-receptor interactions involving myeloid populations. Responders to immunotherapy contributed a larger proportion of the predicted bystander compartment, suggesting an association between bystander T-cell abundance and an immune-responsive microenvironment. BYSTER thus links predicted T-cell antigen specificity to transcriptional states, spatial organization and clinical response, highlighting the potential importance of bystander T cells in tumor immunity.

title: Large Language Model Performance in Structured Data Extraction From Neurosurgical Electronic Health Records: Comparative Benchmark Study.
desc: [JMIR formative research] Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to extract information from electronic health records (EHRs). Given the rapid pace of LLM development, robust scenario-specific benchmarks are essential to evaluate clinical usefulness and support safe deployment. This study aimed to compare contemporary LLMs for structured data extraction from real neurosurgical EHRs written in Czech. In a prospective single-center cohort, 172 hospitalized patients provided informed consent for the use of anonymized EHRs. For each patient, predefined records were collected and concatenated. Ground truth for 35 data points was established by dual extraction with consensus. A standardized prompt requesting JSON output was submitted to 19 LLMs. The primary outcome was overall accuracy; secondary outcomes were category-level accuracy and the proportion of complete machine-readable outputs. A total of 6264 documents were collected (median 33, IQR 25-41 per patient). Ground truth was established with 92.6% initial interrater agreement before consensus. Several models produced complete JSON outputs for 100% of cases (Claude 4.1 Opus, Grok 4, and Gemini 2.5 Flash); GPT-4.1 (DeepSearch) and GPT-5 completed 99.4%. The highest accuracy was achieved by GPT-4.1 (87.6%), followed by GPT-4.5 (85.6%), Claude 4.1 (84.8%), and Grok 4 (84.2%). Accuracy declined by data type: binary (up to 95%), numeric (~89%), multiple-choice (~75%), and short text (~78%). Current LLMs can reliably extract structured clinical information from full, non-English EHRs, while older or smaller models show major limitations. A hybrid workflow-automated extraction with targeted validation-appears practical for research use.

title: Auditable AI agents for verifiable end-to-end scientific analysis
desc: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents are evolving from research assistants into end-to-end executors, yet their capacity to generate conclusions at scale outpaces rigorous verification. Here we introduce an auditability-centred paradigm for scientific automation, wherein trust relies not on generative capability or self-evaluation, but on whether claims can be independently traced to primary evidence, reviewed and corrected. Moving beyond post-hoc checks, we embed verification throughout the research lifecycle via four principles: grounded knowledge, bounded execution, evidence-backed results and independent verification. We instantiate this paradigm in EvoTrace for viral evolutionary analysis. Distilling peer-review critiques and methodological literature, we curated 13 principles, 236 pitfalls and 50 analytical units - validating 47 across a six-tier hierarchy - to encode methodological limits as executable constraints. Across simulated benchmarks, six viral datasets and an end-to-end Crimean-Congo haemorrhagic fever virus (CCHFV) study, claim-evidence auditing compiled evidence packages for all 233 analyses (flagging 26 incomplete evidentiary chains), while independent numerical and figure audits rectified 17 flaws, including three blocker-level errors. For CCHFV, EvoTrace intercepted a data-contradictory claim, recalibrating 'no reassortment candidates' to 'no high-confidence candidates'. By co-delivering verification evidence, auditable automation shifts AI-driven science from autonomous generation to continuous scrutiny and correction.

Artificial Intelligence for Auditory Electrophysiological Biomarkers in Alzheimer's Disease and Hearing Loss: A Critical Narrative Review.
desc: [Bioengineering (Basel, Switzerland)] Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder with a long preclinical phase, making early biomarker discovery essential for timely diagnosis, risk stratification, and intervention. Hearing loss has increasingly been recognized as a clinically important and potentially modifiable factor associated with cognitive decline and dementia risk. Beyond peripheral auditory impairment, accumulating evidence suggests that central auditory dysfunction, altered auditory processing, and electrophysiological abnormalities may emerge during the course of AD and related cognitive disorders. Auditory electrophysiological signals, including electroencephalography (EEG), auditory event-related potentials (ERP), auditory evoked cortical potentials (AECP), auditory brainstem response (ABR) recordings, cochlear microphonics (CM), and distortion product otoacoustic emission (DPOAE) measures, provide objective and repeatable measurements of peripheral and central auditory pathway function. However, conventional analysis based on peak latency, amplitude, spectral power, and manually engineered features may not fully capture subtle disease-related alterations distributed across time, frequency, and waveform morphology. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers new opportunities to extract high-dimensional and physiologically informative representations from auditory and neural signals. Machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), self-supervised learning (SSL), explainable artificial intelligence (XAI), and multimodal modeling can support data-driven biomarker discovery, especially in settings where labeled datasets are limited and electrophysiological changes are subtle. This critical narrative review synthesizes current knowledge at the intersection of hearing loss, AD, auditory electrophysiology, and AI. We discuss traditional signal processing, supervised ML, deep neural networks, self-supervised representation learning, explainable models, and multimodal integration strategies. We also identify major methodological limitations, including small sample sizes, heterogeneous acquisition protocols, insufficient external validation, limited interpretability, data leakage risks, and challenges in translating animal-model findings to human disease. Finally, we propose future directions for trustworthy, interpretable, and multimodal AI systems capable of advancing auditory electrophysiological biomarkers for AD and hearing-related neurodegeneration.

title: RIPPLE: learning nucleotide relations in an RNA foundation model
desc: RNA function depends on interactions between nucleotides that can be widely separated in sequence, yet capturing these relationships remains challenging for RNA language models. Existing approaches primarily learn nucleotide relationships implicitly from individual nucleotide reconstruction or rely on external structural information to model nucleotide interactions. Here we introduce RIPPLE, an RNA foundation model that learns to identify and represent sparse, predictively useful nucleotide relationships directly from sequence. Pretrained on 32.4 million RNA sequences, RIPPLE uses pairwise predictive utility to guide relational learning, transferring training-time supervision into a sequence-only model without requiring structural inputs at inference. RIPPLE improves overall performance across five downstream tasks spanning RNA family classification, ribosome loading prediction, secondary-structure prediction, three-dimensional contact prediction, and splice-site recognition. Mechanistic analyses further show that utility-guided learning improves the recovery of informative interactions and enhances the transferability of learned RNA representations.

The Translation Gap in Artificial Intelligence-Based Renal Mass Characterization: A Narrative Review.
desc: [Cancers] Artificial intelligence (AI) models for solid renal mass characterization show promising discrimination in multicenter and some prospective test sets, yet little published evidence supports their routine clinical use. We examine four translation gaps. Independent, representative validation remains limited, and most studies use resected, pathologically confirmed masses, underrepresenting small indeterminate lesions managed by biopsy or surveillance. Recent multicenter models, including RenalCLIP and MPANet, broadened tasks and external testing but remain retrospective. Four retrospective reader experiments suggest that AI assistance can improve readers' accuracy or consistency, but no study identified measured effects on management or patient outcomes. Regulatory evidence is limited: one renal tool reported by its manufacturer as certified under the European Union Medical Device Regulation rests on a single-center retrospective reader study of detection and reporting, and no characterization device was identified in the U.S. Food and Drug Administration AI-enabled device list. The 2026 European Association of Urology guidelines discuss AI as an emerging technology without a graded recommendation. Cost, information technology integration, trust, and interpretability further restrict adoption. We propose a roadmap built around one intended use, the small indeterminate solid mass considered for biopsy or surveillance, with prespecified thresholds, target-specific reference standards, and paired management and safety endpoints.

Artificial Intelligence for the Molecular Diagnosis of Kidney Diseases: From Computational Pathology to Noninvasive Multi-Omics.
desc: [Bioengineering (Basel, Switzerland)] Creatinine, estimated glomerular filtration rate and histology detect kidney disease late and say little about the molecular heterogeneity driving progression. Artificial intelligence can extract molecular features from biofluid omics; digitised biopsies and retinal images supply proxy readouts, not molecular measurements. In this review we grouped the literature by histopathology, multi-omics, foundation models and noninvasive systems and checked each result against its cohort, endpoint and validation setting. Reported performance is often high, but most results come from retrospective single-cohort evaluations; external and prospective validation are uncommon, and we found no study among those reviewed showing improved patient outcomes. High discrimination therefore establishes technical performance only; clinical utility and patient benefit remain untested. The evidence to date supports feasibility, not benefit, and the weakness lies in evaluation design rather than model architecture. The evidence so far establishes feasibility, not benefit. Until prospective studies on shared external cohorts are available, these tools are best used to augment existing diagnostic practice, with patient outcomes as the measure of success.

title: More than a Second Pair of Eyes: Artificial Intelligence Across the Breast Imaging Pathway.
desc: [Diagnostics (Basel, Switzerland)] Artificial intelligence (AI) is moving from stand-alone accuracy studies to prospective deployment across breast screening, risk prediction, multimodal diagnosis, treatment response, and workflow support. The goal of this narrative review is to determine which AI applications have demonstrated clinical benefit, which remain technically promising, and what safeguards are required for implementation. We synthesize randomized trials, prospective cohorts, real-world implementations, external validations, systematic reviews, and guidance identified in PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus through 30 June 2026. In screening, AI-supported mammography can increase cancer detection and reduce reading workload, but effects depend on whether AI is used as concurrent support, an independent reader, triage, or partial autonomy; autonomous workflows may shift work and cost downstream through additional recalls. MASAI met its prespecified noninferiority criterion for interval cancer, but this should not be interpreted as proof of equivalence or mortality benefit. Image-based risk models often discriminate better than density or conventional clinical models, although prospective benefit from AI-guided allocation to supplemental imaging has not yet been demonstrated. Evidence for contrast-enhanced mammography (CEM), MRI, ultrasound, radiomics, and multimodal models is less mature and limited by external validation, domain shift, missing data, operator dependence, and uncertain incremental value beyond clinicopathological factors. Ungrounded large language models and opaque foundation models are not suitable for autonomous clinical advice. Current evidence therefore supports controlled, task-specific integration rather than radiologist replacement; real clinical benefit depends on governance of the whole AI-enabled pathway, including local validation, human factors, downstream resource use, statistical stopping rules, and fallback procedures.

Advances in PET/CT Segmentation for Lymphoma: Bridging Classical Approaches With Artificial Intelligence.
desc: [Molecular imaging] Accurate segmentation of metabolically active lymphoma on whole-body 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography (18F-FDG PET/CT) is important for prognosis and treatment planning. Conventional methods show substantial variability, whereas deep learning (DL) offers improved automation but limited multicenter generalizability. To compare classical and AI-based segmentation approaches and assess their clinical performance, reproducibility, and potential for precision oncology. A structured search of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, EMBASE, and Google Scholar (1990-2025) identified studies on lymphoma segmentation using manual, threshold-based, region-growing, clustering, atlas-based, or DL methods. Outcomes included Dice similarity coefficient (DSC), reproducibility, and prognostic relevance. A total of 73 studies were included in the final analysis. Threshold-based methods were simple but inconsistent. Region-based approaches achieved DSCs of approximately 0.80-0.84, while clustering methods reached about 0.87. Atlas-based techniques improved physiologic uptake exclusion but often required expert review. DL models, particularly U-Net and V-Net variants, achieved DSCs of approximately 0.75-0.88 and approached expert-level performance. Hybrid PET/CT and longitudinal models further improved segmentation accuracy. AI-based segmentation offers scalable and reproducible lymphoma burden assessment. Key challenges remain multicenter generalizability, small-lesion detection, and explainability, highlighting the need for harmonized datasets and clinically oriented validation.

From innovation to implementation: perspectives from Chief Health AI Officers.
desc: [npj health systems] Drawing on perspectives from interviews with four pioneering chief health artificial intelligence officers (CHAIOs), this editorial examines how executive AI leadership transforms health systems. Insights reveal CHAIOs combine technical fluency in AI with clinical and operational expertise to drive impact. As the use of health AI expands, interviewees emphasize that specialized leadership is not only essential for effective AI governance but also critical for its safe and sustainable use.

title: Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence for Biomedical Applications-3rd Edition.
desc: [Bioengineering (Basel, Switzerland)] The integration of machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI) into biomedicine has rapidly evolved from proof-of-concept algorithmic experimentation to fully operational decision-support frameworks and precision-medicine applications [...].

title: From Generative Biology to Evidence-Centric Drug Discovery.
desc: [Pharmaceuticals (Basel, Switzerland)] Generative and predictive artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly increasing the number of molecular, structural, cellular, and therapeutic hypotheses that can be explored computationally. Experimental capacity, however, has not expanded at a comparable rate. The result is an evidence bottleneck, in which biological hypotheses are generated faster than they can be experimentally tested, reproduced, and translated. This mismatch is particularly consequential for pharmaceutical discovery, where computational predictions alone cannot establish biological function, mechanism, or therapeutic value. As the number of computationally generated hypotheses grows, the central challenge shifts from candidate generation to the prioritization of hypotheses for experimental validation. This evidence bottleneck represents a defining constraint of AI-enabled biological discovery. We examine how different biological claims, including structural, interaction, functional, mechanistic, and therapeutic claims, require distinct types and levels of evidence. We also address the cost and context-dependence of experimental validation. Furthermore, we discuss how information-guided experimental design and iterative model-experiment feedback can improve the allocation of limited experimental capacity. We propose an evidence-centric framework for drug discovery that extends the evaluation of generative models beyond their ability to generate or rank hypotheses. The framework emphasizes experimental testability, mechanistic understanding, reproducibility, and translation into actionable biological and therapeutic knowledge.

title: Deep Learning-Assisted COF-Based Hydrogel Platform for Point-of-Care Monitoring and Photothermal Treatment of Infected Wounds.
desc: [Advanced healthcare materials] Non-real-time monitoring in diabetic wound infections often leads to treatment delays, exacerbating tissue damage and impairing healing. Herein, this study develops a deep learning-assisted covalent organic framework (COF)-based wound management platform for point-of-care pH monitoring and photothermal therapy. The platform is constructed using a multifunctional hydrogel, covalently incorporating methacrylated phenol red (MA-PR) for stable pH colorimetric sensing and integrating metal-free COF-102 as a photothermal therapeutic unit. Benefiting from its extended π-π conjugated framework and low thermal conductivity, COF-102 achieves efficient photothermal conversion without the need for metal ions or additional photothermal agents, thereby enhancing the biosafety of the system. Furthermore, a convolutional neural network (CNN) is introduced to analyze hydrogel color images, enabling accurate classification of wound status and supporting near-infrared photothermal intervention. The model is deployed on a mobile web application, facilitating convenient point-of-care analysis. In an infected wound animal model, the platform shows good therapeutic performance, reduces unnecessary heat exposure, and significantly promotes wound healing. Overall, this study establishes a point-of-care wound management strategy for photothermal therapy of chronic wounds.

title: Death, Existentialism, and the Personalised Patient Preference Predictor.
desc: [Bioethics] It has recently been proposed that fine-tuned large-language models (LLMs) could more accurately predict the preferences of incapacitated patients than surrogates. This hypothetical technology has been named the personalised patient preference predictor (P4). Advocates of the P4 claim that the P4 will not only more accurately predict patient preferences, but will better respect patient autonomy, facilitate the composition of advance directives, and reduce the emotional burden of surrogate decision-making. I challenge these purported benefits by arguing that the P4 would pose a substantive risk to our ability to meaningfully grapple with death. Drawing on the philosophies of Søren Kierkegaard and Martin Heidegger, I argue that adopting an existential attitude towards death is central to the pursuit of an ethical life. Implementation of the P4 risks inhibiting both patients and surrogates from adopting an existential attitude towards death, with deleterious consequences.

title: POSNNET: Positioning Neural Network Estimation Tool.
desc: [Sensors (Basel, Switzerland)] Many applications rely on IMU and GNSS data for localization, typically fused using algorithms such as the Kalman filter or its variants. Although this approach provides accurate localization without requiring additional infrastructure, its performance degrades in GNSS-denied environments. Deep learning methods have been proposed to address this issue in real time; however, because they do not leverage future data, they yield suboptimal reconstructions in applications that do not require real-time processing. To overcome this limitation, we introduce POSNNET, a post-processing framework designed to reconstruct position and velocity during prolonged periods of weak or absent GNSS signals. POSNNET is intended for localization scenarios in which real-time processing is not required, including sports performance analysis, infrastructure-free road mapping, and wildlife tracking, although its applicability across these domains requires further validation. The framework estimates velocity using state-of-the-art neural networks that leverage both past and future IMU and GNSS data. Position is subsequently recovered through weighted bidirectional integration. To improve reconstruction accuracy and consistency, the outputs of multiple neural networks are combined. POSNNET was validated offline against causal real-time baselines using simulated GNSS outages in a 100-h outdoor equestrian dataset characterized by higher speeds and more complex dynamics than typical pedestrian motion, with the sensor-fusion output serving as the reference trajectory. It achieved average trajectory errors, relative to this reference, of 4.07 m for simulated GNSS outages lasting from 30 s to 2 min and 7.06 m for outages lasting from 2 to 5 min, corresponding to an 93.4% (for outages lasting 30 s to 2 min) and 95.6% (for outages lasting 2 to 5 min) improvement in accuracy over the strongest evaluated real-time state-of-the-art method.

title: AI Identity Threat and Job Crafting Among University Teachers.
desc: [Behavioral sciences (Basel, Switzerland)] Generative artificial intelligence can challenge teachers' professional self-evaluations, yet how these concerns relate to subsequent work behavior remains unclear. We examined AI identity threat, supervisor-directed feedback seeking, and individual job crafting in a three-wave study at two universities in central China (n = 563 at baseline). The behavioral measures were adapted to an AI-related work context. A multiple-indicator random-intercept cross-lagged panel model separated stable differences between teachers from fluctuations within teachers. Higher-than-usual threat was associated with greater subsequent feedback seeking in both intervals (β = 0.428 and 0.398). Feedback seeking was associated with subsequent job crafting in the second interval (β = 0.553), whereas evidence in the first interval was inconclusive (β = 0.194, p = 0.130). The specific T1 threat-T2 feedback seeking-T3 crafting sequence showed a positive prospective indirect association (b = 0.266; 95% Monte Carlo CI [0.112, 0.459]). The feedback-to-crafting coefficients differed statistically, but unequal observation intervals and possible academic-calendar influences limit interpretation of this difference. The findings suggest that teachers' requests for supervisory feedback may connect AI-related identity concerns with later work adjustment.

title: ASKG: Adaptive Spatio-Temporal Knowledge Grounding for Candidate-Constrained Point-of-Interest Recommendation.
desc: [Entropy (Basel, Switzerland)] Candidate-constrained point-of-interest (POI) recommendation asks a large language model (LLM) to infer a user's next destination from an ordered trajectory and a fixed set of candidate descriptions. The model expresses its decision by generating the corresponding candidate label. Unlike item recommendation, this task must reconcile semantic preference with physical reachability and changes in visit intent. However, existing retrieval-augmented methods often select evidence by text similarity and serialize graph facts as independent sentences. They can consequently retrieve a topically relevant but geographically implausible venue and lose the relations that explain how a candidate fits the user's current context. We propose Adaptive Spatio-Temporal Knowledge Grounding (ASKG) to carry visit-relevant POI evidence from retrieval to label generation. ASKG adjusts graph-semantic and geographic recall to the user's activity range, gives greater weight to evidence associated with recent visits, and preserves typed relations within a fixed graph-token budget. The candidate prompt then queries these graph tokens directly. A candidate-aligned objective trains the LLM to distinguish among the valid labels. It is a weighted combination of full-vocabulary language modeling and a cross-entropy loss restricted to the n valid candidate labels. Under a candidate-constrained protocol with 10 options on Yelp and 20 on Foursquare, the reported experiments with three LLM backbones per dataset show that ASKG attains the highest MRR in all six dataset-backbone settings and the highest ACC in five. On average across the six dataset-backbone settings, ASKG achieves a relative improvement of 5.9% in MRR and 8.3% in ACC over the strongest baseline.

title: Artificial intelligence capacity in the rural United States: a national qualitative study.
source: PubMed · Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
desc: [Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA] To understand how rural hospitals use artificial intelligence (AI) and identify ways to reduce the barriers to safe, effective use of high-quality tools that align with these hospitals' key priorities. Stratified random sample drawn from the full population of critical access hospitals (CAHs) in the United States in 2025 (n = 1377) to approximate proportional representation of the 4 census regions. We conducted in-depth qualitative interviews with hospital leadership (eg, CMIOs, CIOs, IT leads) tasked with decision-making about technology. Interviews were conducted between October 20, 2025, and January 23, 2026. Drawn from the full population of CAHs in the US in 2025, 256 hospitals were sampled and interviews were completed for a total of 50 CAHs represented by 73 interview participants. Generative AI applications were more common and seen as more valuable for CAH contexts than traditional predictive AI. Primary barriers included infrastructure limitations, cost, and lack of transparency on how AI tools worked. Despite a desire to implement robust governance, most CAHs did not have the ability to do so and reported a critical need for information, tools, and policies to build their AI governance capacity. Information (peer learning, information from non-commercial sources), tools (registries, model cards), and policy to support technical capacity were perceived as the most responsive ways to build capacity. To reduce structural barriers to safe and effective AI decision-making, resources and investment should focus on information sharing with and across rural organizations, AI governance support, and transparency efforts. This will support CAHs in judiciously leveraging available resources and prevent waste on low-quality or misaligned AI tools.

title: Artificial intelligence-guided selection of adjuvant chemotherapy and survival in gastric cancer.
source: PubMed · Gastric cancer : official journal of the International Gastric Cancer Association and the Japanese Gastric Cancer Association
desc: [Gastric cancer : official journal of the International Gastric Cancer Association and the Japanese Gastric Cancer Association] Selecting adjuvant chemotherapy for gastric cancer requires balancing tumor risk and patient-related factors. We developed and internally validated a recurrent deep survival machine (RDSM) framework to evaluate whether concordance with AI-recommended treatment is associated with overall survival (OS). This retrospective cohort study analyzed 15,848 patients with stage II-III gastric cancer from the Japanese Gastric Cancer Association (2011, 2013). Patients receiving neoadjuvant therapy, non-standard regimens, or dying within 8 weeks post-surgery were excluded. Patients were categorized as AI-recommended or AI-non-recommended based on whether their treatment matched the model-derived recommendation (the regimen with the highest predicted 5-year survival probability). Primary outcome was 5-year OS. Model performance was evaluated using the concordance index (C-index), and multiple imputation with propensity score overlap weighting (MI-OW) was used for the observational comparison of treatment concordance. RDSM showed superior discrimination compared with the Cox model (C-index, 0.77 vs. 0.73). After MI-OW, concordance with AI-recommended treatment was associated with higher 5-year OS than discordance (74.00% vs. 66.16%; adjusted difference, 7.84 percentage points [95% CI, 6.06-9.62]). A similar association was observed among patients aged ≥ 75 years (64.18% vs. 52.76%; adjusted difference, 11.42 percentage points [95% CI, 6.72-16.12]). These associations are not causal treatment effects. SHAP analyses highlighted patient-related factors for S-1 monotherapy and tumor burden for S-1 plus oxaliplatin. RDSM identified model-derived treatment patterns associated with observed OS differences, without establishing benefits from AI-guided treatment changes. External validation and prospective evaluation are needed before clinical use.

title: 瑞旭集团助力杭州莱恩瑟特两款内窥镜产品成功获批韩国 MFDS 注册证
Advances in Multimodal Imaging and Artificial Intelligence for the Diagnosis and Management of Diabetic Retinopathy: From Biomarkers to Personalized Care.
desc: [Medicina (Kaunas, Lithuania)] Background and Objectives: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) remains a leading cause of preventable vision loss. Staging based on colour fundus photography captures only part of a disease that involves the whole neurovascular unit and the retinal periphery. This narrative review summarizes the structural (optical coherence tomography, OCT), vascular (OCT angiography and ultra-widefield imaging) and functional (microperimetry, electrophysiology) biomarkers of DR, grades the evidence supporting each of them, and examines how artificial intelligence (AI) is changing screening, prognostication and treatment selection. Materials and Methods: PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus and Web of Science were searched for publications from January 2000 to May 2026, giving priority to randomized trials, prospective multicentre cohorts, systematic reviews and externally validated algorithms. Results: Among imaging biomarkers, disorganization of the retinal inner layers, outer retinal integrity and ultra-widefield angiographic non-perfusion have the most consistent prognostic evidence, whereas OCT angiography metrics remain device-dependent. AI has progressed from research classifiers to autonomous systems with regulatory authorization in the United States and the European Union, to prospectively evaluated deployments in national programmes and low-resource settings, and to time-to-event progression models and foundation models. Image-based prediction improves discrimination over clinical risk factors by modest margins, and biomarker-guided treatment of diabetic macular oedema still rests largely on retrospective series. Cross-device standardization of quantitative metrics, representative datasets, prospective outcome trials and health-economic evidence remain the main gaps. Conclusions: Individualized screening intervals are the application closest to routine practice, whereas phenotype-driven therapy and precision monitoring remain promising but unproven.

title: 华为发布首款维感 G1 动态血糖仪，售价299元起
Generative AI-Driven Interpolation of Cross-Family Kinase Space: Discovery of Dual-Targeting Degraders of IRAK4 and TYK2.
desc: [Journal of medicinal chemistry] Bridging structural discontinuities between disparate protein families is a fundamental challenge in multi-target design. We present a generative artificial intelligence (AI) platform for the non-linear interpolation of cross-family kinase space to simultaneously modulate innate (interleukin-1 receptor-associated kinase 4, IRAK4) and adaptive (tyrosine kinase 2, TYK2) immunity. Utilizing a variational autoencoder-recurrent neural network (VAE-RNN) model within the POLYGON framework, we successfully navigated high-dimensional latent space through an iterative "sampling-scoring-refocusing" strategy. This approach bypassed the geometric limitations of traditional pharmacophore merging, leading to the rational discovery of a novel spirocyclic scaffold with significant structural novelty (Tanimoto similarity <0.45). Integration of WaterMap-based optimization and proteolysis-targeting chimera (PROTAC) conjugation yielded C-8-014, a potent dual-target degrader achieving nanomolar potency and efficient degradation of both kinases. This study demonstrates a validated closed-loop methodology for navigating "unreachable" regions of the kinome, providing a paradigm-shifting approach for cross-family chemical design and a powerful molecular tool for chemical biology.

title: Dual-Model Collaboration with Consistency Calibration for Intelligent Acupuncture Prescription Recommendation.
source: PubMed · Chinese journal of integrative medicine
desc: [Chinese journal of integrative medicine] A dual-model collaborative framework for intelligent acupuncture prescription recommendation was proposed. Specifically, symptom-to-acupoint mapping was formulated as an end-to-end text generation task and an intelligent recommendation method based on dual-model collaboration with consistency calibration (DM3C) was proposed. By combining a domain-fine-tuned generator, retrieval-augmented LLM outputs, and a consistency-calibrated random forest filter, the proposed DM3C enhances the generalizability and recall of intelligent acupuncture prescription recommendations, these findings demonstrate its potential as an auxiliary acupoint recommendation tool.
